page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 CPU with 4 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. A key hardware component is the single bundled NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which provides 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark performance tradeoff between CPU-bound and GPU-accelerated workloads. Standard CPU and memory operations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, consistently fall into the bottom 25% of performance. Similarly, memory bandwidth and database operations are relatively weak. However, the integrated NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance in the top 10% for large language model inference. Specifically, prompt processing and text generation for both small 135M and medium 7B models achieve high throughput, such as 2296.42 tokens per second for 7B prompt processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-4 is highly optimized for GPU-centric workloads rather than general-purpose compute. Utilizing this instance for CPU-heavy tasks represents a poor resource-to-cost tradeoff due to its weak CPU performance. Conversely, for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployment, and GPU-accelerated graphics tasks, the hardware profile offers excellent qualitative value by pairing a highly capable 24 GB VRAM GPU with a modest, budget-friendly CPU and memory configuration.
